slides.title: You made it, it is yours
slides.text: A drawing you make is yours, because you made it. Finding something online does not make it yours. The maker decides how their work may be used.
slides.alt: A letter from Ava from Class: “Can I put your owl drawing on our class poster? I will write your name under it. Is that okay with you?”

focus.cue: Ava asks first: may she use your drawing?
Ava from Class: someone you know

slides.title: Read the badge
slides.text: Every piece of work carries a simple badge. Some badges say ask first, and some say give credit. Public domain work is free for anyone.
steps: credit badge: use it and give credit

slides.title: Photos need a yes
slides.text: Sharing a photo of someone else needs their yes, always. If a friend posts a photo of you that you do not like, ask them to take it down. If it stays up, tell a trusted adult, who can help report it.
slides.alt: A game chat from Max with both clues marked: “I posted that photo of you with spaghetti on your face.” and “I will not take it down.”

focus.cue: A photo of you, posted without your yes
It stays up: tell a trusted adult

slides.title: My keep-private rule
slides.text: Some things stay private, always: your address, your school and your passphrase. Say your own rule out loud. These are mine to keep.
slides.alt: A game chat from Fun Quiz with clues marked: your first pet, the street you grew up on and your birthday; share your result with everyone!

focus.cue: A quiz fishing for your street and birthday
These stay private: mine to keep

slides.title: The Magpie's nest
slides.text: The Magpie pins photos of other birds in its nest without asking. Now the other birds have stopped visiting. Asking first is how sharers keep their friends.

words.means: a yes from the maker to use their work
picking one thing instead of another

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Trick Inbox at Ask First and sort all 6 messages: whose yes does each one need? Then write the credit line for a game you might make. Last, name one thing you keep private.
slides.alt: A group chat with three clues marked: “Post that funny photo of Sam asleep on the bus!”, “He will never know.” and “Everyone will laugh.”

focus.cue: Play Ask First: whose yes does it need?
